boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten verified, under-21-safe ways to gather around Grinnell without paying admission or making a purchase.

cards.title: Browse the Museum of Art Together
cards.subtitle: A free gallery hang inside the Bucksbaum Center for the Arts
cards.notes: Meet inside Bucksbaum, browse the current exhibitions together, and leave time to compare one artwork each person noticed.
cards.short_summary: Share an unhurried art-viewing session in the college’s public museum.
cards.evidence_claim: Grinnell College states that the Grinnell College Museum of Art is free and open to all.
cards.access_notes: Free and open to all. Check the official visit page for current semester hours before going.

cards.title: Take a CERA Nature Walk
cards.subtitle: Public trails at Grinnell College’s 365-acre field station
cards.notes: Coordinate a ride, bring water, and choose hiking, bird-watching, photography, sketching, or another quiet nature activity.
cards.short_summary: Spend a social afternoon exploring a college field station beyond campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Grinnell College says CERA is open to the public for hiking, bird-watching, photography, painting, drawing, and quiet enjoyment.
cards.access_notes: Public access is documented by the College; the site is about 11 miles from campus, so arrange transportation and review the trail map.

cards.title: Catch a College Theatre Production
cards.subtitle: Free public performances with advance ticket reservations
cards.notes: Check the production calendar, reserve free tickets through the box office, and review any posted content notice with your group.
cards.short_summary: Make an evening of a student or departmental stage production at Bucksbaum.
cards.evidence_claim: The Grinnell College box-office FAQ states that tickets are free and performances are open to the public, with rare exceptions.
cards.access_notes: Tickets are free but should be reserved; sold-out performances may offer a door waitlist. Minors must be accompanied by an adult.

cards.title: Gather at Central Park
cards.subtitle: Downtown green space with a shelter, stage, and accessible playground
cards.notes: Bring your own snacks or skip food, claim an open lawn spot, and use the playground or walking paths without reserving a shelter.
cards.short_summary: Meet downtown for an easy lawn, playground, or conversation hang.
cards.evidence_claim: Grinnell College’s visitor guide states that City of Grinnell neighborhood parks are free and available for public use and identifies Central Park’s amenities.
cards.access_notes: Use of the public park requires no admission or purchase. Do not reserve facilities that carry a separate rental charge.

cards.title: Walk the Ahrens Park Loop
cards.subtitle: A 1.5-mile outdoor path through a multi-use public park
cards.notes: Start near a shelter, walk the 1.5-mile path at a conversational pace, then use an open court or green space if available.
cards.short_summary: Turn a public park loop into a low-key walking meetup.
cards.evidence_claim: Grinnell College states that city parks are free for public use and describes Ahrens Park’s 1.5-mile walking path, courts, fields, and green spaces.
cards.access_notes: Walking and ordinary public-park use require no purchase. Some areas may be unavailable during construction; avoid the paid driving range.

cards.title: Play Pickleball at Ahrens Park
cards.subtitle: Four outdoor public courts at Ahrens/Paschall Memorial Park
cards.notes: Bring paddles and balls you already own, rotate players through short games, and yield the court promptly when others are waiting.
cards.short_summary: Organize a casual no-fee doubles session on the park’s outdoor courts.
cards.evidence_claim: Grinnell College says city parks are free and available for public use and identifies four pickleball courts at Ahrens Park.
cards.access_notes: No admission or purchase is required for ordinary public-park use; this activity assumes participants bring equipment they already have.

cards.title: Run a Casual Basketball Shootaround
cards.subtitle: Outdoor basketball courts in a free public park
cards.notes: Bring a ball from home, choose HORSE or a relaxed shootaround, and keep the group small enough to share space with other users.
cards.short_summary: Use the outdoor courts for a flexible social game without paying admission.
cards.evidence_claim: Grinnell College states that city parks are free for public use and lists outdoor basketball courts among Ahrens Park’s amenities.
cards.access_notes: Ordinary court use requires no admission or purchase; bring a ball you already own and observe any posted closures.

cards.entity_name: Ahrens/Paschall Memorial Park Sand Volleyball Court
cards.title: Set Up a Sand Volleyball Game
cards.subtitle: A public sand court at Ahrens/Paschall Memorial Park
cards.notes: Bring a volleyball you already have, divide into flexible teams, and switch to cooperative rallies if the group is too small for a match.
cards.short_summary: Gather friends for rallies or a casual match on the park’s sand court.
cards.evidence_claim: Grinnell College says city parks are free and available for public use and specifically lists a sand volleyball court at Ahrens Park.
cards.access_notes: No admission or purchase is required for ordinary park use; participants should supply a ball they already own.

cards.title: Walk the Trail at Arbor Lake
cards.subtitle: An 81.4-acre natural-resource park beside the GART
cards.notes: Meet at the east-side trail access, follow the lake edge together, and pause for conversation or nature observation along the route.
cards.short_summary: Pair a waterside walk with time outdoors in a large city natural area.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Grinnell identifies Arbor Lake Park as an 81.4-acre natural-resource area with the Grinnell Area Recreational Trail along its east shore; Grinnell College states city parks are free for public use.
cards.access_notes: General park and trail access requires no admission or purchase. City parks close daily from 11 p.m. to 6 a.m.; shelter rental is not included.

cards.title: Walk Through the Veterans Monument
cards.subtitle: A 42-foot public artwork in Central Park
cards.notes: Approach from the park, follow the spiral pathway into the sculpture’s center, and give the group quiet time for reflection.
cards.short_summary: Visit a walk-through civic sculpture designed as a place of remembrance.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Grinnell identifies the monument as a 42-foot steel sculpture in Central Park with a spiral path leading visitors into an open-air interior.
cards.access_notes: The monument is within Central Park, which Grinnell College identifies among the city parks that are free and available for public use.
